name: InsideBar
quote: inside bar: A bar with a high that is at or below the high of the prior bar and a low that is at or above the low of the prior bar.

book_order_type: n/a (bar classification; often a breakout-mode setup)

notes: Catalog's InsideBar tests bar N ago against N+1; this is the current-bar-vs-prior form, equivalent at lag 0.

name: OutsideBar
quote: outside bar: A bar with a high that is above or at the high of the prior bar and a low that is below the low of the prior bar, or a bar with a low that is below or at the low of the prior bar and a high that is above the high of the prior bar.
description: Shared primitive: the current bar's range engulfs the prior bar's range.
pseudocode: high[0] >= high[1] && low[0] <= low[1]
book_order_type: n/a (bar classification; often a breakout-mode setup)

complexity.reason: two-bar comparison

name: DoubleInsideBar_ii

book_order_type: buy stop above / sell stop below the ii's combined range

name: InsideOutsideInside_ioi

description: Three consecutive bars: bar[1] is an outside bar versus bar[2], and bar[0] is an inside bar versus bar[1].
pseudocode: high[1] >= high[2] && low[1] <= low[2] && high[0] <= high[1] && low[0] >= low[1]
book_order_type: buy stop above / sell stop below the inside bar's range

name: OutsideInsideOutside_oio

pseudocode: high[1] <= high[2] && low[1] >= low[2] && high[0] >= high[1] && low[0] <= low[1]
book_order_type: n/a (bar classification / breakout-mode setup)

complexity.reason: fixed three-bar sequence test

name: OutsideOutside_oo

name: PauseBar
quote: pause bar: A bar that does not extend the trend. In a bull trend, a pause bar has a high that is at or below the prior bar, or a small bar with a high that is only a tick or so higher than the previous bar when the previous bar is a strong bull trend bar.
description: In an up-trend, the current bar's high does not meaningfully exceed the prior bar's high (at/below it, or only a few ticks above a strong prior trend bar). A type of pullback bar.
pseudocode: high[0] <= high[1] + pauseTicks * tickSize

name: LowBarOverlapWithPrior
quote: Not much overlap with the prior bar or bars.
description: Quality filter: the signal bar overlaps the prior N bars' combined range by at most a fraction F.
pseudocode: priorRange = highest(high[1], lookback) - lowest(low[1], lookback); overlap = min(high[0], highest(high[1], lookback)) - max(low[0], lowest(low[1], lookback)); overlap <= overlapFraction * priorRange
book_order_type: n/a (signal-bar quality gate)

name: InsideBodyBar
quote: it was an inside body variant (its body was inside the body of the signal bar, which is a weaker version of an inside bar)

complexity.reason: single-bar-pair comparison of bodies

name: OutsideBarResetsLegCounter
quote: Whenever there is a strong outside up bar that breaks the market into a new trend, its low is the start of the trend and all bar counting gets reset. For example, the two-bar reversal at bar 9 was a low 1 setup and not a low 2.
description: When a strong outside bar breaks the market into a new trend, reset any pullback/leg counter (H1/H2, L1/L2 style) so the outside bar's extreme becomes the new trend start.
pseudocode: high[0] > high[1] && low[0] < low[1] && (close[0] - open[0]) >= bodyFraction * (high[0] - low[0]) => pullbackCounter = 0; trendStartLow = low[0]
book_order_type: n/a (state-reset rule feeding H1/H2/L1/L2 counters)

complexity.reason: an outside-bar test that also mutates persistent counter state used elsewhere

name: PauseBar

name: ThinAreaLowBarOverlap
quote: A thin area is a breakout area where there is very little overlap of the bars.
description: Primitive/continuation: over the last N bars each bar overlaps its prior bar by at most F of the prior bar's range (a thin, one-sided breakout leg).

book_order_type: n/a (leg quality test; the thin area's midpoint is the measured-move midpoint)

name: PauseBarBreakoutEntry
quote: if there is a strong bull move in which the last bar was a small bar with a high just a tick or two below the prior bar's high and that bar was a large bull trend bar and followed one or two other large bull trend bars, if you buy one tick above this bar, you are buying at the high of the day.

pseudocode: OutsideBarPrimitive[2] && InsideBarPrimitive[1] && OutsideBarPrimitive[0] && close[0] > open[0]
book_order_type: n/a (the outside bar is both signal and entry, intrabar); close-based form enters at the next open

complexity.reason: fixed three-bar classification

notes: Contrast with T07-19 IoiPattern (inside-outside-inside), a different bar ordering.

name: FailedBreakoutSmallInsideBarReversal
quote: if the market breaks out to the upside and then the next bar is a small inside bar (its high is not higher than that of the large breakout bar) and then the following bar has a low that is below this small bar, the odds of a failed breakout and a reversal back down increase considerably
description: Long side (mirror of the book's bear example): a bear breakout bar is followed by a small inside bar (its low not below the breakout bar's low), then this bar closes above that small bar's high -- fade the failed breakout upward.
pseudocode: close[2] < open[2] && body(2) >= bodyFraction * range(2) && low[1] >= low[2] && range(1) <= smallFraction * range(2) && close[0] > high[1]
book_order_type: buy stop one tick above the small inside bar's high (book's mirror: sell stop below it)

complexity.reason: three fixed-offset bars, no windows

notes: Book's own example is a bull breakout failing to the downside; mirrored here per the long-side convention.

name: IIPattern
quote: An ii pattern is an inside bar that follows a larger inside bar. It is two in a row with the second being inside the first and of the same size or smaller.
description: Primitive: two consecutive inside bars, the more recent one inside the one before it (Brooks allows either extreme to be equal, per ch6 p137's inside-bar note).
pseudocode: (high[0] <= high[1] && low[0] >= low[1]) && (high[1] <= high[2] && low[1] >= low[2])
book_order_type: n/a (bar-pair classification)

complexity.reason: two chained two-bar inside comparisons

notes: An 'iii' pattern (three inside bars in a row) is the same test extended one more bar; not split into its own candidate.

name: IIPatternBreakoutEntry
quote: traders would buy on a stop at one tick above the second bar.
description: Enter on a breakout of the ii pattern in the direction of the break; the stop is placed beyond the opposite side of BOTH bars, not just the second (signal) bar.
pseudocode: IIPattern[0]
book_order_type: buy stop one tick above max(high[0], high[1]) (long) / sell stop one tick below min(low[0], low[1]) (short); often placed as an OCO bracket in breakout mode, the unfilled side becoming the protective stop

complexity.reason: inherits the trivial IIPattern shape test

name: IOIPattern
quote: An ioi pattern, which is an inside bar followed by an outside bar and then another inside bar (inside-outside-inside).
description: Primitive: bar 2 is an inside bar, bar 1 is an outside bar (relative to bar 2), and bar 0 is an inside bar (relative to bar 1).
pseudocode: (high[2] <= high[3] && low[2] >= low[3]) && (high[1] >= high[2] && low[1] <= low[2] && (high[1] > high[2] || low[1] < low[2])) && (high[0] <= high[1] && low[0] >= low[1])
book_order_type: n/a (three-bar classification)

complexity.reason: chains an inside-bar test, an outside-bar test, and another inside-bar test

name: IOIBreakoutEntry
quote: it is often prudent to place a sell stop below and a buy stop above that second inside bar and enter in the direction of the breakout. The unfilled order then becomes the protective stop.
description: Enter on the breakout of the second (most recent) inside bar of an ioi pattern, in either direction (breakout mode).
pseudocode: IOIPattern[0]
book_order_type: buy stop one tick above high[0] / sell stop one tick below low[0], OCO bracket; the unfilled side becomes the protective stop

complexity.reason: inherits IOIPattern

name: OutsideBar
quote: If the high of the current bar is above the high of the previous bar and the low is below the low of the previous bar, then the current bar is an outside bar.
description: Primitive: bar n is an outside bar, its high above and its low below the prior bar's. A tolerance lets an 'almost outside' bar (p191: 'if something is almost a reliable pattern, it will likely yield the reliable result') qualify.
pseudocode: high[0] >= high[1] - toleranceTicks * tick && low[0] <= low[1] + toleranceTicks * tick && (high[0] > high[1] || low[0] < low[1])
book_order_type: n/a (bar classification)

complexity.reason: two-bar comparison of highs and lows

notes: Chapter 6 p135 gives the looser 'at or beyond' form; toleranceTicks covers both.
Direction-agnostic; 'outside up' = outside bar with a bull body, 'outside down' = bear body.

name: InsideBar
quote: If the bar after the outside bar is an inside bar, then this is an ioi pattern (inside-outside-inside)
description: Primitive: bar 0 is inside the prior bar (Brooks allows one extreme to be equal).
pseudocode: high[0] <= high[1] && low[0] >= low[1]
book_order_type: n/a (bar classification)

complexity.reason: two-bar comparison

notes: Existing InsideBar uses strict inequalities; Brooks (ch6 p137) explicitly allows equality.

name: OutsideBarBreakoutEitherWay
quote: Traditional technical analysis teaches that outside bars are setup bars for a breakout in either direction, and that you should put an entry stop above and below.
description: The prior bar is an outside bar and this bar closes above its high: enter long at the next open (the traditional bracket entry). Brooks says this is usually unwise on 5-minute charts, especially for large outside bars, but it is the baseline the rest of the chapter argues against.
pseudocode: OutsideBar[1] && close[0] > high[1]
book_order_type: buy stop one tick above the outside bar's high (sell stop one tick below its low); unfilled order becomes a reversal order

complexity.reason: two-bar pattern plus a close comparison

notes: Brooks: 'it is usually best to not enter on a breakout of the bar' unless a strong reversal is expected; pair with T07-10 / T07-15 / T07-24 as filters.
Brooks's 'wait for the bar to close and then enter on the breakout of the outside bar' is exactly this close-based form.

name: LargeOutsideBarBreakoutFilter
quote: it is almost always unwise to enter on a breakout of a 5 minute outside bar, especially if the outside bar is large, because of the greater risk that the distant stop entails.
description: Block an entry whose signal bar is an outside bar with a range larger than a multiple of the recent average range (the protective stop would be too far away).
pseudocode: !(OutsideBar[1] && range(1) >= largeMultiple * avgRange(rangeLookback))
book_order_type: n/a (filter)

complexity.reason: average range over a window

name: OutsideBarAsEntryBarAfterGoodSignalBar
quote: If the bar suddenly reverses back above the bull signal bar, the buy stop will be triggered and the current bar will become an outside bar and an entry bar.
description: The prior bar was a bull reversal bar (a decent signal bar) and this bar went below it and then closed back above its high, making it an outside up bar: the buy stop above the signal bar is honored. Enter at the next open.
pseudocode: BullReversalBar[1] && OutsideBar[0] && close[0] > high[1]
book_order_type: buy stop one tick above the signal bar's high, left in place while the next bar trades below the signal bar; filled intrabar as the bar becomes outside up

complexity.reason: two-bar classification and a close comparison

notes: Close-based form gives up the intrabar fill; Brooks's alternative on p196 is to wait for the outside bar's close anyway (see T07-37).
p193: 'As long as the bar before the outside bar is a decent signal bar, entering on the outside bar can be a sensible trade.'

name: NoReversalEntryOnOutsideBarWithoutSignalBar
quote: In general, traders should not enter a reversal trade on an outside bar unless the bar before it was a decent signal bar.
description: Block a long whose entry bar is an outside bar unless the bar before it was a bull reversal bar.
pseudocode: !(OutsideBar[0]) || BullReversalBar[1]
book_order_type: n/a (filter)

complexity.reason: two-bar classification

name: OutsideBarInMiddleOfRangeFilter
quote: If an outside bar is in the middle of a trading range, it is meaningless and should not be used to generate trades
description: Block any entry signaled by an outside bar whose midpoint sits in the middle band of the recent N-bar high-low range (i.e., neither at the top nor the bottom of the range).
pseudocode: mid = (high[1] + low[1]) / 2; rh = highest(high, rangeBars)[1]; rl = lowest(low, rangeBars)[1]; pos = (mid - rl) / (rh - rl); !(OutsideBar[1] && pos > lowerBand && pos < upperBand)
book_order_type: n/a (filter)

complexity.reason: highest/lowest over a window

notes: p189 bar 5 and p194 bar 4: outside bars in sideways overlapping markets are 'just part of the trading range and not a signal bar'.

name: FailedBreakoutOfOutsideBarFade
quote: If the market instead breaks out in the other direction, just let it go and look to fade a failed breakout of the outside bar, which commonly happens within a few bars.
description: An outside bar formed within the last K bars; some bar since then closed below its low (downside breakout) and this bar closes back above that low: buy the failed breakout.
pseudocode: exists k in 2..maxBarsSince: OutsideBar[k] && exists j in 1..k-1: close[j] < low[k]; && close[0] > low[k]
book_order_type: buy stop one tick above the high of the bar that reversed back into the outside bar's range

complexity.reason: variable-offset scan for the outside bar and the breakout bar

notes: p194 bar 6: 'a short following the breakout of the top of an outside up bar' is the mirror.
p194 bar 5: a large bear-body outside bar closing below the prior outside bar's low trapped shorts; the small bull doji after it was the signal for the failed-breakout long.

name: IoiPattern
quote: If the bar after the outside bar is an inside bar, then this is an ioi pattern (inside-outside-inside) and can be a setup for an entry in the direction of the breakout of the inside bar.
description: Inside bar, then an outside bar, then an inside bar (bars 3,2,1); this bar closes above the high of the second inside bar: enter long at the next open. Breakout-mode setup, direction chosen by the breakout.
pseudocode: InsideBar[3] && OutsideBar[2] && InsideBar[1] && close[0] > high[1]
book_order_type: buy stop one tick above and sell stop one tick below the second inside bar; the unfilled order becomes the protective stop

complexity.reason: fixed-offset bar comparisons

notes: Take only when the market can plausibly reach the profit target (p186); see T07-21 for the size/position filter.

name: IoiAtNewExtremeWithReversalBodyInsideBar
quote: if the ioi is at a new swing high and the second inside bar is a bear bar that closes near its low, a downside breakout could be a good short since it is likely a second entry
description: Long side: the ioi's outside bar made a new N-bar low and the second inside bar is a bull bar closing near its high; buy the upside breakout of that inside bar.
pseudocode: InsideBar[3] && OutsideBar[2] && low[2] <= lowest(low, swingLookback)[3] && InsideBar[1] && close[1] > open[1] && (high[1] - close[1]) <= closeNearFraction * range(1) && close[0] > high[1]
book_order_type: buy stop one tick above the second inside bar

complexity.reason: lowest over a window plus fixed-offset bar tests

notes: Brooks reasons this is 'likely a second entry' because the first entry occurred as the outside bar traded beyond the first inside bar.

name: IoiLargeOrCentredInsideBarFilter
quote: The inside bar that followed it (ioi) was too large to use as a breakout signal, because you would be either selling at the bottom of a trading range or buying at the top
description: Skip the ioi breakout when the second inside bar is large relative to the outside bar or its midpoint sits near the middle of the outside bar (barbwire).
pseudocode: !(InsideBar[3] && OutsideBar[2] && InsideBar[1] && (range(1) >= maxInsideFraction * range(2) || abs(((high[1]+low[1])/2) - ((high[2]+low[2])/2)) <= centreBand * range(2)))
book_order_type: n/a (filter)

complexity.reason: fixed-offset arithmetic

notes: p191: 'The bar 2 breakout of the inside bar following bar 1 failed, which is common, especially when the inside bar is large.'

name: WithTrendOutsideBarInFirstLegOfReversal
quote: When a with-trend outside bar occurs in the first leg of a trend reversal and the prior trend was strong, it functions like a strong trend bar and not a trading range type of bar.
description: After a strong bear trend has reversed up, a bar that first trades below the prior bar's low (a higher low) and then closes above the prior bar's high as an outside up bar traps bears: buy. Brooks expects two legs up measured from the bottom of this outside bar.
pseudocode: priorBearTrendStrong && reversalUpUnderway && low[0] > lowest(low, legLookback)[1] && OutsideBar[0] && close[0] > high[1] && close[0] > open[0]
book_order_type: buy stop one tick above the prior bar's high, even if it fills on an outside up bar

complexity.reason: needs prior-trend strength, reversal detection, and a higher-low test against a swing low

notes: p194 bar 2: 'an outside bar up and a possible low of the day since the market was reversing up from a big gap down' — the outside bar is considered the start of the move up.
p197 bar 6 is the mirror image: a failed high 2 long whose entry bar reversed into an outside down bar 'acted like a bear trend bar'.

name: OutsideBarInTrendOnlyWithTrendBreakout
quote: bar 1 was an outside up bar in a strong bear trend, so traders would be looking to enter only on a downside breakout.
description: When the prior bar is an outside bar and the market is in a strong trend, allow only the with-trend breakout: long side passes only if in a bull trend (blocks a long breakout of an outside bar in a bear trend).
pseudocode: !(OutsideBar[1]) || StrongTrendContext.bull
book_order_type: n/a (filter)

complexity.reason: EMA-based trend context

notes: Chapter 6 p170 says the same: an outside up bar 'is not an acceptable long entry in either a trading range or a bear trend'.

name: FailedIoiBreakoutFade
quote: Since traders expected bulls to exit with a loss below the low of bar 2, their entry bar, they shorted at one tick below bar 2, which was a failed ioi breakout at the top of a trading range.
description: Long side: an ioi (bars 4,3,2) broke out downward on bar 1, which was a small bar near the bottom of the ioi range; this bar closes back above bar 1's high: buy the failed breakout (trapped shorts exit above their entry bar).
pseudocode: InsideBar[4] && OutsideBar[3] && InsideBar[2] && close[1] < low[2] && range(1) <= smallFraction * range(3) && close[0] > high[1]
book_order_type: buy stop one tick above the failed breakout (entry) bar

complexity.reason: five-bar fixed pattern with a breakout-then-failure sequence

notes: Brooks: 'Since the ioi bars were so large, there was plenty of room below bar 2 for at least a scalp'.

name: OutsideOutsidePatternFilter
quote: Bar 5 was an even larger outside bar, forming an oo or outside-outside pattern. This is usually just a larger trading range.
description: Two consecutive outside bars (oo): treat as a trading range and block breakout entries off either bar.
pseudocode: !(OutsideBar[1] && OutsideBar[2])
book_order_type: n/a (filter)

complexity.reason: fixed-offset bar tests

name: OutsideBarReversalAtNewExtremeStrongClose
quote: Bar 7 broke to a swing high and reversed down as an outside bar that closed on its low... it would be better to sell below the low of bar 7 since you would be shorting below a strong bear reversal bar
description: Long side: this bar is an outside bar that made a new N-bar low and closed near its high (a strong bull reversal): buy above it.
pseudocode: OutsideBar[0] && low[0] <= lowest(low, swingLookback)[1] && close[0] > open[0] && (high[0] - close[0]) <= closeNearFraction * range(0)
book_order_type: buy stop one tick above the outside bar's high

complexity.reason: lowest over a window

notes: Brooks's earlier alternative (short as the bar traded below the small bear bar before it) is the intrabar version.

name: OutsideBarAfterMajorityBodiesOneWay
quote: Bar 6 was an outside down bar and five of the six prior bars had bear bodies. It closed on its low, and aggressive traders could have shorted below it after such bear strength
description: Long side: this bar is an outside bar closing on its high and at least K of the prior N bars had bull bodies: buy below... i.e., buy above it (with-trend outside bar after accumulated strength).
pseudocode: OutsideBar[0] && close[0] > open[0] && (high[0] - close[0]) <= closeNearFraction * range(0) && count over k in 1..N of (close[k] > open[k]) >= K
book_order_type: sell stop one tick below the outside down bar's low (book example is the short)

complexity.reason: window count of body directions

notes: Brooks adds that it 'trapped bulls into buying the old bull trend, which now may be over' (a failed high 2, p197).

name: OutsideBarReversalAgainstSignalBar
quote: the long entry bar reversed into an outside bar down, trapping longs in and bears out. This outside bar acted like a bear trend bar and not just an outside bar.
description: Long side: the prior bar was a bear reversal bar (a short signal bar) and this bar traded below... i.e., beyond it in the short direction and then closed above its high as an outside bar with a bull body: trapped shorts must cover; buy.
pseudocode: BearReversalBar[1] && OutsideBar[0] && close[0] > high[1] && close[0] > open[0]
book_order_type: buy stop above the outside bar (or at market as it turns outside)

complexity.reason: two-bar classification

notes: Distinct from T07-12: there the outside bar confirms the prior signal bar; here it reverses against it.
'Because it was an outside bar, the entry bar and its failure happened within a minute or two' — the close-based form gives up that speed.

name: IiPattern
quote: The bar 7 ii was a possible final flag.
description: Shared primitive: two consecutive inside bars (bar[0] inside bar[1], bar[1] inside bar[2]).
pseudocode: high[0] <= high[1] && low[0] >= low[1] && high[1] <= high[2] && low[1] >= low[2]
book_order_type: n/a (pattern primitive; Brooks enters on a stop beyond the ii in either direction)

complexity.reason: fixed-offset three-bar comparison

notes: Equals InsideBar(0) AND InsideBar(1) with <= instead of strict.

name: IiFinalFlagAfterBearRunBuy
quote: The bar 7 ii was a possible final flag.
description: An ii pattern forming after a bear run (at least M bear trend bars in the last N bars) is a possible final flag; buy when the bar after the ii closes above the ii's high.
pseudocode: isIi(1) && countTrue(isBearTrendBar(i) for i in 3..lookback) >= minBearBars && close[0] > high[1]
book_order_type: buy stop above the ii high (mechanized: close above it, then next bar open)

complexity.reason: window count plus fixed-offset tests

notes: 'Final flag' proper needs the flag to be the last pullback of a protracted trend — a research-grade context; this mechanization approximates it with a bear-bar count.

name: InsideBarSignalAfterTwoBarReversal
quote: The next bar was a bull inside bar and was a good signal bar for the trend from the open bull.
description: After a two-bar reversal (T11-05), an inside bar is a good with-trend signal bar; buy when a later bar closes above the inside bar's high.
pseudocode: TwoBarReversal(2) && high[1] <= high[2] && low[1] >= low[2] && close[0] > high[1]
book_order_type: buy stop one tick above the inside bar high (mechanized: next bar open)

complexity.reason: chains fixed-offset bar-pattern tests with no persisted state

name: LowBarOverlapWindow
quote: If the rally is in a very tight, steep channel with no pullbacks and very little overlap between the bars, and the rally goes far above the bull high before having any pause or pullback, the momentum is strong
description: Momentum filter: the average overlap between consecutive bars over the last windowBars, as a fraction of the prior bar's range, is at most maxOverlap. Low overlap = strong momentum; its negation (many overlapping bars) flags a weak test likely to form a lower high (p259).
pseudocode: overlap(i) = max(0, min(high[i], high[i+1]) - max(low[i], low[i+1])) / (high[i+1] - low[i+1]); average over i in 0..windowBars-1 of overlap(i) <= maxOverlap
book_order_type: n/a (context)

complexity.reason: window average of a two-bar quantity

notes: p270: 10 bear trend bars with little overlap and large bodies with small tails were climactic; combine with T15-52 for the climax reading.

name: IIPattern
quote: They could have shorted below the ii pattern at bar 18, or on any of the several following bars, as the market became always-in short.
description: Primitive: two consecutive inside bars (bar[1] inside bar[2], bar[0] inside bar[1]). The entry is a stop beyond the second inside bar; close-based: the next bar closes above high[0] of the ii (long) / below its low (short).
pseudocode: high[1] < high[2] && low[1] > low[2] && high[0] < high[1] && low[0] > low[1]
book_order_type: stop one tick beyond the ii

complexity.reason: three fixed-offset bars

notes: InsideBar covers one inside bar; ii is two. The direction is taken from the breakout, which makes the pattern itself direction-agnostic.

name: LittleOverlap
quote: very little overlap between adjacent bars, and small tails. This is the spike phase of a trend
description: Shared primitive: the current bar overlaps the prior bar by no more than a fraction of its own range (bull form: the low is at or near the prior bar's close/high).
pseudocode: (min(high[0], high[1]) - max(low[0], low[1])) <= overlapFraction * (high[0] - low[0])
book_order_type: n/a (bar classification)

complexity.reason: two-bar arithmetic

notes: Overlap of ranges is direction-agnostic, hence sides=same; Chapter 19 gives the sharper bull form low[0] >= close[1] - tick.

name: InsideBarIsPullback
quote: Any bar or series of bars that represents any pause or loss of momentum is a pullback, even if there is no actual backward movement. This includes a single inside bar
description: In a bull spike, a single inside bar counts as a pullback (a pause bar): buy when the bar after the inside bar closes above the inside bar's high.
pseudocode: high[1] <= high[2] && low[1] >= low[2] && BullSpikeEndedAt(2) && close[0] > high[1]
book_order_type: buy stop one tick above the inside bar high

complexity.reason: inside-bar test plus the spike window loop

name: AverageBarOverlapFraction
quote: with lots of overlapping bars, several bear bodies
description: Two-sidedness sign: the average range overlap between consecutive bars over the last windowBars exceeds overlapFraction of the bar range. Long filter: require it below the threshold.
pseudocode: average((min(high[i], high[i+1]) - max(low[i], low[i+1])) / (high[i] - low[i]), windowBars) < maxOverlapFraction
book_order_type: n/a (context)

complexity.reason: window average of a two-bar ratio

name: BarOverlapFraction
quote: a series of trend bars with little overlap
description: Primitive: the fraction of the current bar's range that overlaps the prior bar's range; 'little overlap' is this fraction below a threshold. Used by spike, tight-channel and weak-channel tests.
pseudocode: overlap = max(0, min(high[0], high[1]) - max(low[0], low[1])); overlapFrac = overlap / (high[0] - low[0]); overlapFrac <= maxOverlap
book_order_type: n/a (bar classification)

complexity.reason: two-bar arithmetic

name: PauseBar
quote: By definition, the spike ends immediately before the first pause bar or pullback because it is the pause that signifies the end of the spike.
description: Primitive: in a bull move, a pause bar is the first bar that fails to make a higher high, or has a bear body, or is an inside bar. It marks the end of a spike.
pseudocode: high[0] <= high[1] || close[0] < open[0] || (high[0] <= high[1] && low[0] >= low[1])
book_order_type: n/a (structure primitive)

complexity.reason: two-bar comparisons

name: InsideBarBreakoutPullback
quote: Other traders bought above the bar 5 breakout pullback setup (an inside bar is a pause and, therefore, a type of pullback)
description: Entry: bar[2] broke out (closed above the highest high of the prior N bars), bar[1] is an inside bar, and the current bar closes above the inside bar's high.
pseudocode: close[2] > highest(high, breakoutLookback)[3] && high[1] <= high[2] && low[1] >= low[2] && close[0] > high[1]
book_order_type: buy stop one tick above the inside bar

complexity.reason: window highest plus fixed-offset comparisons

notes: Equals InsideBar(1) + CloseAbovePriorHigh(1) + a breakout term on bar 2.

name: TripleInsideBarFlag
quote: it led to a bull flag (an iii pattern) as expected
description: Entry: in a bull trend, three consecutive inside bars (each inside the one before) form a flag; buy when a bar closes above the high of the first (largest) inside bar.
pseudocode: inside(1,2) && inside(2,3) && inside(3,4) && close[0] > high[1]  /* inside(a,b) = high[a] <= high[b] && low[a] >= low[b] */
book_order_type: buy stop above the pattern high

complexity.reason: fixed-offset comparisons

notes: Also ii (two inside bars) with insideCount 2.

name: NoPauseByFourthBarIncreasesReversalOdds
quote: If the market does not pause by the third or fourth bar, it might have gone too far too fast, and this increases the chances that the market will reverse instead of trend.
description: Filter/context: if the first N bars of the session all extended in the same direction with no pause (no inside bar, no bar failing to make a new extreme), weight countertrend/reversal setups a bit higher for the next few bars instead of assuming trend continuation.
pseudocode: barsIntoSession >= noPauseBars && all of bars 1..noPauseBars made a new session extreme with no pause bar
book_order_type: n/a (context filter)

complexity.reason: a short backward scan of session-relative bars against the pause-bar primitive

chapter_title: Trend from the Open and Small Pullback Trends
